items.title: Netflix's Live Content Push: Can it Sustain Subscriber Growth?
items.summary: Netflix's selective live events strategy is boosting subscriber sign-ups, engagement and ads, positioning live programming as a key growth driver.

items.title: Canada to Cease Compelling U.S. Streamers to Help Finance Domestic Broadcasting
items.summary: Canada will abandon efforts to compel foreign streamers to make mandatory financial contributions to the domestic entertainment industry, according to a court filing.

items.title: Scoop: People Incorporated explores sale of The Daily Beast again
items.summary: People Incorporated, formerly known as IAC, is exploring a possible sale of The Daily Beast as it looks to focus its portfolio around People Inc. and MGM, sources told Axios.

items.title: The Profit Engine That Could Power Netflix Stock's Next Rally
items.summary: The stock has slid over the past year even as the company's margins reached a three-year peak and management guides them higher, and that gap is the upside case.

items.title: Billionaire Investor Andreas Halvorsen’s Top 5 Picks: Are They a Buy Now?
items.summary: Viking Global just filed its 13F, handing retail investors a five-stock shortlist that spans AI chips, streaming turnarounds, and a rate-cycle trade, and four of them are flashing buy signals before the next earnings window closes.

items.title: Disney or Salesforce: Which Beaten-Down Dow Giant Is the Smarter Dip-Buy?
items.summary: Both Salesforce and Disney have taken serious hits this year, but retirement investors face a genuine dilemma when the cheaper stock and the faster-growing stock point in opposite directions. Picking the wrong dip could cost you more than just patience.

items.title: YouTube’s Peacock Partnership is a Streaming Bundle Breakthrough
items.summary: For YouTube, the partnership is the latest and greatest attempt to trounce Netflix as both seek to become all-in-one entertainment platforms.

items.title: Warner Bros. Stock Hits Lowest Price Since Paramount Deal: Merger Odds Around 50%
items.summary: Warner Bros. Discovery  stock Monday hit its lowest point since the company’s merger with  Paramount Skydance  was reached in February as Wall Street appears to be putting little more than a 50% chance that the deal will get done.  Warner Bros. stock dropped 1.8% Monday to $25.28, ending about 18% below the $31-a-share cash offer from Paramount, whose stock also declined Monday.  Warner Bros. stock had been trading around $27 in June.
